summary.text: Alexander Fagan is One Nation's candidate for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he is a director of a technology company based in Melbourne with global operations, that he earlier worked in consulting, and that he holds engineering and science degrees from the University of Melbourne. One Nation's candidate page refused automated access, so it could not be checked.

sources.title: Brighton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Anthony Hain is the Libertarian Party's candidate for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian election. A chess player who holds FIDE's Candidate Master title (awarded in 2015), he teaches and coaches the game, and he also competes in racquetball and squash, taking out the top grade of the national racquetball circuit in 2017. His campaign says he grew up around Brighton and became politically active in 2020 in response to Melbourne's lockdowns.

priorities.text: Mandatory remand for repeat violent offenders after a second offence, and filling police vacancies
Opposing any widening of laws that police speech
Never voting for a tax increase, and cutting land tax and stamp duty
Paying down state debt by cutting waste rather than raising taxes

summary.text: Barry Vincent is the Family First candidate for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he spent more than 40 years in the Victorian public service, starting at the Health Commission of Victoria in 1979 and ending as a logistics adviser in emergency management at the Department of Health before retiring late in 2022. In retirement he volunteers with two charities that help people in hardship and victims of family violence.

occupation.text: Retired public servant (health policy and emergency management)

prior_roles.role: Special Projects Officer, Health and Medical Unit
Program Adviser – Logistics in Emergency Management, Response and Recovery

priorities.text: Protecting human life, and recognising the biological difference between men and women
Traditional family values, freedom and the safety of women and children
Preserving Australia's culture and way of life

summary.text: Bridget Mullahy is standing for Labor in Brighton at the 2026 Victorian election. A business consultant, she also lectures at Deakin University and RMIT University. Labor says she has worked for more than two decades with leaders and organisations on change programs in health, education and business. A Bridget Mullahy stood for Labor in Port Phillip's South Melbourne Ward at the 2024 council elections, but no source seen confirms it is the same person.

occupation.text: Business consultant and university lecturer (Deakin University and RMIT University)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's 2024 results list a Labor candidate of this name; no source seen links her to the 2026 Brighton candidate.

priorities.text: Better schools and education
Good-quality health care
Help with the cost of living for people in Elwood, Hampton and Brighton

summary.text: Ebony Bain is the Greens candidate for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian election. She is an outreach learning facilitator at Museums Victoria, and she has a background in science communication. On her party page she describes herself as a renter living in the Bayside area.

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressures, including housing, groceries and health care
Stronger action on climate change
Working with local residents to find solutions together

summary.text: James Newbury has been the Liberal member for Brighton since 2018. He was Shadow Treasurer from January to October 2025 and is now Shadow Attorney-General and Manager of Opposition Business. He is seeking re-election in Brighton in 2026.

occupation.text: Company secretary in financial services and political adviser

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Environment and Climate Change
prior_roles.note: Parliament gives the start as February 2022; Wikipedia gives September 2021.

prior_roles.role: Senior adviser to Premier Denis Napthine

faction.name: Liberal moderate

Opposing unsuitable development
Protecting the area from crime
Looking after the natural environment
A fair share of services and infrastructure for the area

summary.text: Jessica Smith is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian election. She has lived in Hampton for over ten years and has taught at several primary schools in the area. She says she has been a socialist throughout her adult life and has campaigned on marriage equality, Palestine and refugee rights, and against the far right.

priorities.text: I think we need well-funded, top tier public services that leave no Victorian behind.
Fully funding public schools, including repairs to run-down school buildings
Building much more public housing, and keeping it well maintained
More frequent, better-connected public transport
Paying for services by taxing billionaires and large corporations

sources.title: Brighton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jessica Smith, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: John Casley is standing as an independent for Brighton at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. An independent of the same name stood in Brighton at the 2018 and 2022 state elections; the ABC's 2022 results table lists him as John Tiger Casley, with 0.6 per cent of first preferences. Neither the ABC nor any other source we found had published a biography of him as at 9 Nov 2026.
